name: Remove automatic sync ownership arbitration pipeline

current_round.prompt:
From: Buddy Williams <buddy.williams@insurity.com>
Subject: Remove automatic sync ownership arbitration pipeline

Body:
Request: Remove automatic sync ownership arbitration pipeline. Goals stay where they are transferred unless manually moved via surface (CLI, web UI, etc.)
Details:
Found it. The Refine 4.2.0 binary (deployed today at 09:13) introduced a new automatic sync ownership arbitration pipeline. Here's exactly what happened and why:

  Why they moved: The commit message explains it directly — before 4.2.0, whenever two nodes had conflicting state on the same goal, the sync would wedge and require a manual operator. This was causing mass blockage at scale (67 unresolved
  path(s) in production). So 4.2.0 added an auto-resolve rule: "the node that owned the record at the last agreed baseline is authoritative."

  Your 35 failed goals were originally assigned to the default node (the QA machine, bo2lnxnevo04). This node (bo2lnxipsapp01) had picked them up and advanced them through the workflow — but at the last sync baseline, default was the
  declared owner. When 4.2.0's sync ran, it saw the conflict, applied the baseline-ownership policy, and moved those goals back to default.

  Where they went: The default node — which now has 56 failed goals (up from 16 before). Your 35 plus others from around the fleet that were similarly repatriated.

  They're not lost — they're on default in failed state. The catch is that they're also still carrying the signal schema failure (guidance_applied string vs integer) from the 4.2.0 agent prompt mismatch. So they'll keep failing on default
  too until that's fixed.



[cid:insurity-small2_2f81c33c-d951-4e5c-a467-1113541ca22c.jpg]
Buddy Williams
Buddy.Williams@insurity.com

goal.name: Remove automatic sync ownership arbitration pipeline

governance.constitution:
- Refine's components are model (entities), process (supervisor to manage running processes), prompts (LLM templates), surfaces (interfaces into refine), tools (reusable functions for workflow steps), and workflow (defined workflow which calls out to tools). These map directly to src/[model| process|prompts|surfaces|tools|workflow].
- Refine uses a flat file persistence, file-based indexes, in-memory caching, and Rust to maintain high performance. Ensure <50ms performance on CLI and API calls (assuming we are not waiting on LLMs or outside tools).
- Ensure that the architecture is maintained and is consistent. Do not invent new architectural concepts; instead, follow the existing architecture.
- Ensure that documentation, especially src/intent/*, is maintained and the existing document format is preserved.
- Ensure Refine remains "agent-first" by using installed coding-agent CLIs. Do not duplicate coding agent functionality.
governance.product: Refine is a local-first, agent-first operating layer for software delivery. It moves user-defined Goals through a workflow to ensure parallel implementation across Nodes, quality, and governance.

rules.text: Keep component code within `src/{model,process,prompts,surfaces,tools,workflow}` and extend existing architecture instead of inventing new concepts.
Preserve Rust-based flat-file persistence, file indexes, and in-memory caching; keep non-external CLI/API work under 50ms.
Update affected documentation—especially `src/intent/*`—without changing its established format.
Use installed coding-agent CLIs for coding-agent capabilities; do not reimplement them.

guidance_candidates.instructions: Use the Goal and the relevant files under docs/intent/ as the durable product context. Preserve the Foundation, Capabilities, and Surfaces boundaries; shared capability ownership; thin and semantically consistent surfaces; local inspectable state; and recoverable Git and process behavior. Update only the affected docs/intent pages when the change alters documented product intent or an architectural contract. Do not require unrelated documentation, cleanup, or broader work.
guidance_candidates.name: Intent and architecture
guidance_candidates.rule: Apply when a Goal changes Refine product behavior, architecture, shared capabilities, durable state, workflow, or a surface contract.

guidance_candidates.instructions: Keep each code file focused on one cohesive responsibility. Treat roughly 500 lines as a prompt to review structure, not as a blind hard cap. When a file grows because it mixes responsibilities or unrelated method families, split it into clearly named modules or files and move methods, helpers, types, and tests with the responsibility they serve. Prefer real module boundaries and stable public APIs over arbitrary chunks or include-only shards. Preserve behavior during structural refactors, and document any justified exception for generated or intrinsically cohesive files.
guidance_candidates.name: Cohesive code files
guidance_candidates.rule: Apply whenever an agent adds or changes code files in any language.

agent_context.workflow_summary: Refine gives this Goal Agent an isolated worktree and a finalized implementation plan. Implement the current Round and report evidence; a separate agent will review and correct the candidate in Quality, then an independent Governance gate will verify policy and integrate the exact passing commit before human Review. Do not directly advance Goal state, approve, merge, or push.

findings.description: P5 excludes docs/runbooks/manage-fleet.md, which currently tells operators that ordinary divergence and contested first contact converge automatically and only opted-out nodes need manual authority.
findings.recommendation: Add docs/runbooks/manage-fleet.md to P5 and rewrite its contested-sync procedure so every unresolved ownership conflict remains failed until an operator chooses authority through a supported surface.

result.summary: The plan is implementation-ready after adding the affected fleet-management runbook to its documentation scope.

checklist.description: Remove the background worker's post-conflict automatic recovery branch, merge-base ownership decision helper, and daemon-only recovery activity so an unresolved sync remains failed with its stable conflict evidence and backoff state instead of invoking terminal recovery.

Constrain deterministic and agent-assisted state resolution to preserve an unambiguous one-sided Goal transfer, escalate concurrent conflicting owner changes for a manual surface decision, and remove the merge-base-owner doctrine that can repatriate a Goal.
Retire state_sync_auto_recovery across defaults, validation, stored-setting migration, and the web runtime settings control while preserving explicit sync authority and Goal transfer surfaces.
Replace the worker and fleet simulation scenarios that expect automatic convergence with contracts for stable transferred ownership, fail-closed unresolved conflicts, and explicit operator recovery.

Update only the affected Fleet, Persistence Sync, CLI, API, activity-evidence intent pages and the state-sync recovery runbook to document manual ownership movement and the remaining resolution boundary.

result.summary: State sync will stop making automatic ownership decisions so explicit Goal transfers propagate without being reversed, ambiguous ownership conflicts remain visible for a surface-driven decision, and the obsolete fallback setting, activity contract, and documentation are removed.
